_readme: Channel definitions for kawasaki_logger.py. You can edit these in the app's Channels tab.
pid: hex local identifier sent as '21 <pid>'. every: read on every Nth update (1 = every time).
formula variables: A B C D... (data bytes), raw, sraw, n, d. Functions: abs min max round signed(v,bits) math.*
verified: set true once a channel's scaling has been checked against a known-good reading.
gauge_min / gauge_max: range of the tile's gauge bar. null = scale to the values seen this session.

priority: phone apps only (iOS and Android). true gives this channel a dedicated re-read between every other channel read, for gauges that need to track faster than 'every' alone allows. Defaults to false; ignored by the Windows app.

pids.name: Engine RPM
pids.notes: Was 'raw' with no scaling (unverified default). At base idle on a 2007 Ultra LX, raw read 306 while the ski's actual idle is ~1200 rpm — 306 * 4 = 1224, a close match. This ECU appears to store RPM in units of 4 rpm per count (opposite of standard OBD-II's PID 0x0C, which divides by 4). Confirmed at one data point (idle); would be good to confirm at a second RPM (e.g. a brief rev) to rule out a non-multiplicative offset.

pids.name: Throttle sensor
pids.notes: Ultra LX: closed = 246 and wide open = 912 counts (about 1.2 V and 4.5 V if 10-bit at 5 V). Use Capture 0 % / 100 % in Edit to set your own ski's values. Carries over to a 2024 SXR160: a 2026-10-16 key-on/engine-off log moving the throttle lever by hand 0-100% read 247 counts closed and 884-885 at full lever travel, close enough to the Ultra LX's 246/912 that no formula change is needed. 884-885 may be short of true mechanical WOT since this was a hand sweep with the engine off, not a full-throttle pull under load.

pids.name: Intake Pressure
pids.notes: This ski has only one physical pressure sensor (in the intake manifold) — no separate barometric sensor. PID 0x05 is that live reading: in a 2026-10-13 idle/rev research log it read ~101.7 kPa at key-on/engine-off (atmospheric), dropped to ~58 kPa once the engine started and settled into idle (manifold vacuum), then rose to ~79 kPa during a rev to 4284 rpm (vacuum partially collapsing). PID 0x08 previously held this channel but was found frozen at a constant 101.8 kPa for the entire session regardless of engine/RPM state — a dead/duplicate register — and was removed. every bumped from 10 to 1 since this is a fast-changing signal, not a slow one like true barometric pressure. Also checks out on a 2024 SXR160: a 2026-10-16 key-on/engine-off log read 836-837 counts (103.66-103.79 kPa, a sane atmospheric value), and 0x08 again mirrored 0x05 exactly at every sample — the same dead/duplicate-register pattern as the Ultra LX. Still need an idle/rev or water-test log on this ski to confirm 0x05 actually drops into vacuum range once the engine runs.

pids.name: Engine temp
pids.notes: Reads degrees C plus 40 (62 = 22 C = 72 F in a 70 F garage). One point only: check against an infrared thermometer once it's warm. Units of C make it switchable between C and F. Seen on a 2007 Ultra LX with key on and engine off. Check on your own ski. A 2026-10-13 water test on another ski showed this channel staying a sane 59-70 C through a sustained 6000+ rpm run while that ski threw an OILH (oil temp high) warning — so on that ECU at least, 0x06 is not the oil sensor; see PID 0x98 below. Also read a sane ambient value on a 2024 SXR160 at key-on/engine-off (60 counts = 20 C, 2026-10-16 log) — consistent with this formula, though unconfirmed under heat on this ski.

pids.name: Intake air temp
pids.notes: Same encoding as engine temp. Seen on a 2007 Ultra LX with key on and engine off. Check on your own ski. Also sane on a 2024 SXR160 at key-on/engine-off (61 counts = 21 C, 2026-10-16 log).

pids.name: Oil Temp
pids.notes: Found via the full-scan Research Log, not in the original kline.py defaults. In a 2026-10-13 water test, this ski threw an OILH (oil temp high) dash warning and backed off from a sustained ~6200 rpm / 42 mph cruise to idle at t=117s, never recovering for the rest of the session. PID 0x98, decoded with the same raw-40 convention as 0x06/0x07, climbed 142C -> 135C -> 153C over that same run, peaking right as the warning apparently hit — while 0x06 ('Engine temp') stayed a boring 59-70C the whole time. Also at t=116.8s, PID 0x02 flipped one bit (0x40->0x42 in its first byte) and latched there for the rest of the session, which looks like a fault/status flag turning on at the same moment. Strong circumstantial case for 0x98 = oil temperature, but unverified — confirm with an infrared thermometer at the oil tank/cooler next time OILH comes on, watching this channel live. At key-on/engine-off on a 2024 SXR160 (2026-10-16), 0x98 read 60 counts (20 C) — the same as Engine temp at that instant, which is expected before the engine runs and doesn't yet distinguish oil from coolant on this ski. Needs a running log to separate them, the way the Ultra LX water test did.

pids.name: Battery
pids.notes: Re-enabled with a corrected divisor. Previously switched off because PID 0x0A returned 00 00 on an Ultra LX at key-on, and a short 2026-10-13 idle/rev research log on another ski showed it 'frozen' right up to engine shutoff — but 0x0A wasn't a defined/polled channel at the time, so it was only sampled once via the slow extra-PID sweep, not actually confirmed static. A later water-test research log, with 0x0A re-read many times over a 2+ minute ride, shows it tracking RPM: raw 695 (13.63 V) at a 6100 rpm cruise, dropping to raw 654-668 (12.82-13.10 V) at idle, rising again on the next cruise — a charging-system signature (alternator output rises with RPM), and raw/51 lands it right in the 13.0-13.7 V range expected while running. Still just a 4-point fit, not calibrated — confirm against a multimeter on the battery terminals next time out. At key-on/engine-off on a 2024 SXR160 (2026-10-16), 0x0A read 0 too, same as the Ultra LX at key-on — consistent so far, but this ski hasn't been run with 0x0A enabled yet to check the raw/51 scaling against RPM.
